Two weeks after fire tore through Laredo's DoubleTree hotel, the ruins have officially become a federal case. ATF fire investigators are expected to arrive in Laredo on Thursday, Oct. 22, to join the investigation into the blaze, according to Mayor Victor D. Treviño — and the city has formally asked the state for heavy-collapse help, according to KGNS.

The site remains under an emergency declaration and continues to be classified as an active collapse site, the city said, with structural safety described as critical while investigators work to determine what caused the fire.

City personnel are now coordinating with federal and state partners as resources are requested and deployed. The city has submitted State of Texas Assistance Requests (STARs) to the Texas Division of Emergency Management — including potential help from Texas Task Force 1 personnel with structural-collapse capabilities like shoring and stabilization. That deployment has not been confirmed.

The city said weekly updates will be provided as personnel arrive and requests are confirmed.

The escalation matters for more than the burned-out building. The DoubleTree sits in the middle of downtown Laredo, where the collapse zone has already strangled neighboring businesses for weeks — and with ATF on the way and the state on call, the wait for answers is only getting longer.

Sources: KGNS (By Ellie Bednarz and Mariana Flores-Sosa), Oct. 21, 2026; Laredo Morning Times (Maria Ruiz), Oct. 21, 2026.

title: ATF arrives Thursday: DoubleTree fire probe goes federal as state aid is requested
